purpose: Compliance matrix consumed by Vizzie to (a) decide whether a dataset may be ingested, (b) render required attribution on maps, embeds and exports, (c) set per-portal crawl rates.

ingest_policy_values.allow: Ingest and serve normally with attribution.
ingest_policy_values.allow_with_flag: Ingest, but surface a share-alike warning to the user before export/publish.
ingest_policy_values.link_only: Do NOT ingest. Show metadata and link to the source portal.
ingest_policy_values.block: Do not surface for ingest at all.

resolution_order: 1. Dataset-level licence from the portal API (normalised via licence_aliases).
2. If absent/unmappable -> portal.default_licence (only where the portal publishes a blanket licence).
3. If still absent -> UNDECLARED (ingest policy: link_only).
usage.attribution: Render licences[<id>].attribution_template with {title} {publisher} {retrieved}. Attribution is non-removable at every tier for the SOURCE; only Vizzie branding is removable.

PUBLIC-DOMAIN.name: Public domain (publisher declaration)
PUBLIC-DOMAIN.attribution_template: {title} — {publisher}, released into the public domain. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
PUBLIC-DOMAIN.note: A publisher's bare 'Public Domain' declaration, which is the single most common licence value on the Socrata network (260 of 911 sampled datasets, 15 Sep 2026 — NYC, Seattle and CDC all use it). Deliberately its own class rather than an alias of US-PD or CC0-1.0: US-PD is specifically the 17 USC §105 federal-works carve-out and does not describe a city portal, and CC0 is a specific legal instrument the publisher did not necessarily execute. This class claims only what the publisher actually said — no rights reserved — so attribution is not required, though the template still offers one.

SEMCOG-CLA.name: SEMCOG Copyright License Agreement
SEMCOG-CLA.attribution_template: {title} — Copyright © SEMCOG. All Rights Reserved. Reproduction or Use Without Permission is Prohibited. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
SEMCOG-CLA.note: A bespoke agreement, read in full 2026-09-19, covering everything on SEMCOG's Hub: clause 1(a) grants a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use, reproduce, modify, distribute, publish, transmit, display and create derivative works, so it is more permissive than its name suggests and commercial use is not restricted. The condition is clause 2(a): every use must carry the copyright notice verbatim, in a reasonably prominent position — which is why this is a class with a fixed attribution_template rather than UNDECLARED. The agreement's example notice carries a year ('Copyright © 2019 SEMCOG'); the template omits it because the year belongs to the work, not the retrieval, and SEMCOG does not publish a per-dataset copyright year. Clause 1(b) excludes third-party rights, so a dataset SEMCOG merely redistributes is not covered by this grant.

OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL.name: Open Government Licence – Canadian province or municipality
OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL.attribution_template: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – {publisher}. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL.note: Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Yukon and the Northwest Territories each publish their own Open Government Licence, all modelled on the federal OGL 2.0. Three texts have now been read in full: Ontario's (19 Sep 2026) and the NWT's (20 Sep 2026) both grant a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual licence to copy, modify, publish, adapt and distribute for any lawful purpose, explicitly including commercial purposes, conditional on acknowledging the source. Yukon's and NWT's own portals declare the licence by name and URL on every dataset (open.yukon.ca: 3,840 of 3,841; opendata.gov.nt.ca: 340 of 341); Alberta's and BC's rest on open.canada.ca's licence register, and Alberta's page 403s a server fetch. One class rather than seven because they differ only in the licensor, and the attribution wording each mandates — 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – <licensor>' — is exactly what {publisher} fills in. Deliberately NOT here: Manitoba's OpenMB licence and Saskatchewan's SUUDL, which are differently-named instruments (SUUDL has its own class), and Vancouver's and Toronto's municipal licences, whose texts are still unreachable — see the resolve.test.ts case that keeps them UNDECLARED.

SK-SUUDL-2.0.name: Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence 2.0
SK-SUUDL-2.0.attribution_template: {title} — Contains information licensed under the Government of Saskatchewan Standard Unrestricted Use Data Licence (Version 2.0). Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
SK-SUUDL-2.0.note: Read in full from the licence PDF (20 Sep 2026): a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to copy, modify, publish, translate, adapt and distribute 'for any lawful purpose', explicitly 'including for commercial purposes'. The one condition is the attribution statement, which the licence dictates verbatim and which this template reproduces. Not folded into OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL: despite near-identical wording it is a differently-named instrument, and the attribution it mandates names itself rather than an Open Government Licence. Covers 334 of the 456 datasets on Saskatchewan's hub plus 413 on open.canada.ca.

STATCAN-OPEN.name: Statistics Canada Open Licence
STATCAN-OPEN.attribution_template: {title} — Source: Statistics Canada, {publisher}. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the permission of Statistics Canada. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
STATCAN-OPEN.note: Read in full 20 Sep 2026: a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use, reproduce, publish, distribute or SELL the Information and value-added products, and to sublicence. Its conditions are accuracy, no implication of StatCan endorsement, no misrepresentation of the source, and no re-identification. Attribution is marked required here because 'not misrepresent the Information or its source' plus StatCan's standard citation practice amount to a source-credit obligation. It turns up on Canadian municipal hubs wherever census-derived layers are republished — 116 datasets on Brampton and 60 on Peel alone.

KITCHENER-ODL.name: City of Kitchener Open Data Licence
KITCHENER-ODL.attribution_template: {title} — {publisher}, City of Kitchener Open Data Licence. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
KITCHENER-ODL.note: Read in full 20 Sep 2026: a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence covering copying, modifying, publishing, translating, adapting and distributing in any medium or format, and it says explicitly 'This includes for commercial purposes'. Unusually it also says 'you are not required to credit the City of Kitchener', which is why attribution_required is false — the template still offers a credit line. Not folded into OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL precisely because of that: the OGL family's one condition is the attribution this licence waives.

MISSISSAUGA-TOU.name: City of Mississauga Open Data Terms of Use
MISSISSAUGA-TOU.attribution_template: {title} — {publisher}, City of Mississauga Open Data Terms of Use. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
MISSISSAUGA-TOU.note: Read in full from the terms PDF (20 Sep 2026): a world-wide, royalty-free, non-exclusive, REVOCABLE licence to use, modify and distribute the datasets in all current and future media and formats for any lawful purpose. Credit is encouraged but not required. The revocability is the reason this is its own class rather than an alias of anything: the grant can be withdrawn, which nothing in the CC or OGL families does. Compare Moncton's near-identical template, which omits the right to modify entirely — see the sources.ts note on why Moncton is not connected.

LDA-UY-0.1.name: Licencia de Datos Abiertos – Uruguay 0.1
LDA-UY-0.1.attribution_template: {title} — {publisher}, Licencia de Datos Abiertos – Uruguay. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie. Reformatted and geocoded.
LDA-UY-0.1.note: Read in full from AGESIC's licence PDF (20 Sep 2026). The grant is explicit about commercial use ('para uso comercial y no comercial') and covers reproduction, distribution, publication, translation, adaptation and transformation, and merging with other data to form new independent datasets. Its condition is the 'Nota de Origen': cite the provider's name, name the Licencia de Datos Abiertos – Uruguay, and identify the dataset — and changes, edits or redesigns must be stated, which is why indicate_changes is true. Covers 2,663 of the 2,717 datasets on catalogodatos.gub.uy under the licence id 'odc-uy'.

portals.label: Statistics Norway (SSB) — StatBank
portals.tos_note: Official statistics; blanket reuse terms for the whole database.
portals.licence_source: Portal default only — PXWeb exposes no per-table licence field

rate_limit.note: Published by the instance itself at ?config: maxCalls=300 per timeWindow=60s (= 5.0/s), maxCells=800000. Read live 19 Sep 2026.

portals.notes: CC BY 4.0 verified 19 Sep 2026 on SSB's API page. GEOGRAPHY IS THE WEAKEST OF THE THREE HERE and the figure is easy to overstate: SSB's Region dimension carries 952 codes, 356 of which appear in GISCO LAU 2021 — but 114 of those 356 are codes SSB itself labels as historical (Halden 2020-2023), leaving only ~242 CURRENT municipalities that join. The gap is Norway's 2024 county split, which recoded the 30xx range (Halden moved 3001 → 3101, and 3101 is absent from the 2021 vintage). A newer boundary vintage than GISCO 2021 is needed before Norwegian data joins cleanly; Sweden (290/290) and Finland (287/288) have no such problem.
